title: Pure Spin Bulk Photovoltaic Effect in an Altermagnetic Higher-Order Topological Insulator
authors: Sibgat Ulah, Ankan Bhattacharyya, Manisha Thakurathi
abstract: We investigate the bulk photovoltaic effect (BPVE) in a $PT$-symmetric two-dimensional heterostructure consisting of a topological insulator coupled to a $d$-wave altermagnet. To describe the symmetry-enforced degenerate bands of this system, we develop a non-Abelian formulation of the spin BPVE, extending the conventional theory from isolated nondegenerate bands to $PT$-degenerate manifolds. We show that the orientation of the Néel vector controls both the topological phase and the character of the nonlinear optical response. When the Néel vector lies in the $xy$-plane, the heterostructure realizes a second-order topological insulator (SOTI) protected by $C_{4z}T$ symmetry. The system also retains $C_{2z}$ symmetry, which completely suppresses second-order charge photocurrents while allowing finite spin photocurrents. As a result, the BPVE becomes an intrinsically pure spin photovoltaic effect, generating a dc spin current without an accompanying charge current. We find that linearly polarized light drives a spin shift current, whereas circularly polarized light generates a spin injection current. Both responses undergo a sign reversal whenever the local Dirac mass changes sign. As the Néel vector is rotated toward the $z$-axis, the SOTI phase transforms into a first-order topological insulating phase, leading to the coexistence of charge and spin photocurrents. Our results establish $PT$-symmetric altermagnetic topological-insulator heterostructures as a versatile platform for generating and controlling pure spin photocurrents and reveal nonlinear spin transport as a sensitive probe of topology and magnetic symmetry.
summary: This paper theoretically investigates the pure spin photovoltaic effect in an altermagnetic topological insulator heterostructure. By developing a non-Abelian theory, the authors show that specific magnetic symmetries can suppress charge currents entirely, leading to a purely spin-generating response. This establishes the material as a versatile platform for controlling nonlinear spin transport using light.
main_problem: The study investigates the Pure Spin Bulk Photovoltaic Effect (BPVE) in a complex magnetic heterostructure to understand spin current generation without accompanying charge currents.
main_result: The system realizes an intrinsically pure spin photovoltaic effect when the Néel vector is in the $xy$-plane, generating dc spin currents controllable by light polarization and magnetic symmetry.
method: The authors develop a non-Abelian formulation of the spin BPVE, extending theory to PT-degenerate manifolds, and analyze response tensors using symmetry constraints.
model_or_system: The model is a PT-symmetric 2D heterostructure combining a topological insulator with a d-wave altermagnet. The Hamiltonian incorporates SOC and magnetic exchange fields, leading to FOTI or SOTI phases depending on the Néel vector orientation.
key_observables:
Pure spin photocurrent ($\sigma_{s,\mu;
u\lambda}$), charge photocurrent, spin shift current (driven by linear polarization), and spin injection current (driven by circular polarization).
important_parameters: Orientation of the Néel vector ($\hat{n}_s$), local Dirac mass sign change, and symmetry protection ($C_{4z}T$ vs $C_{2z}$).
main_assumptions: The theory extends conventional BPVE to PT-degenerate manifolds using a non-Abelian formalism; approximations are made regarding the spin-current operator's applicability in nonlinear optical processes.
figures_summary: Figure 1 schematically shows optically induced spin transport components based on Néel vector orientation. Figure 2 illustrates energy spectra showing FOTI and SOTI topological phases under open boundary conditions.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by defining the physical system (TI/Altermagnet heterostructure), developing the generalized non-Abelian theory for spin BPVE, analyzing how symmetry dictates the pure spin response in different topological regimes (SOTI vs FOTI), and concluding with the platform's potential for controlling spin currents.
why_interesting: The work provides a detailed theoretical framework linking magnetic order parameters (Néel vector) to specific quantized electronic responses (pure spin photocurrents) in topological materials, which is highly relevant for spintronics and quantum optics applications.
